source_excerpts.text:
Let H(g)=H0+g V+g^2 W be self-adjoint for the admitted real g. P:C^d -> H is
an isometry, H0 P=E P, and P^dagger V P=0. Assume a finite-rank map U1 with
P^dagger U1=0 satisfies

 (H0-E)U1=-VP.                                           (1)

The columns must lie in the domains needed below. Define

 K=P^dagger(VU1+WP),
 S=VU1+WP-PK.                                           (2)

For self-adjoint V,W and exact (1),

 K=-U1^dagger(H0-E)U1+P^dagger W P=K^dagger.

P^dagger S=0. Put A=H0-E and, for delta>0,

 Pi_delta=1_{[-delta,delta]}(A),
 U2_delta=-A^(-1)(I-Pi_delta)S.                           (3)

This is an actual bounded spectral multiplier applied to finite source
columns. It is not a physical energy filter. Assume its columns belong to
D(V) intersect D(W); membership in D(H0) follows directly from (3).

For J=P+gU1+g^2 U2_delta, exact multiplication gives

 H(g)J-J(EI+g^2K)
   =g^2 Pi_delta S
    +g^3(VU2_delta+WU1-U1K)
    +g^4(WU2_delta-U2_delta K).                         (4)

Hence at T=hbar tau/g^2, uniformly 0<=t<=T,

 ||exp(-iH(g)t/hbar)P-P exp[-i(EI+g^2K)t/hbar]||
 <=2[|g| ||U1||+g^2||U2_delta||]
   +tau[||Pi_delta S||
         +|g| ||VU2_delta+WU1-U1K||
         +g^2||WU2_delta-U2_delta K||].                 (5)

One may combine orthogonal contributions in quadrature when proved, but the
sum bound (5) is general. This is the full output-isometry norm, so an
arbitrary entangled reference is included. Outside-code probability <=epsilon^2
and unhalved diamond distance <=2epsilon. All escaped amplitudes remain data.

2. A gap-free sufficient condition at second order
-------------------------------------------------

Assume V and W are bounded for the simplest version. If

 1_{ {E} }(H0) S=0,                                    (6)

then ||Pi_delta S|| ->0 as delta->0. Strong convergence suffices because S
has finite-dimensional domain. Taking delta=|g|^alpha with any 0<alpha<1
gives ||U2_delta||<=||S||/delta and makes every other term in (5) vanish.
Thus the finite code operation exp(-i tau K) is obtained with error o(1),
even when the source S has NONZERO continuous spectral density at E and the
formal exact second-order vector -A^(-1)S is nonnormalizable.

For relatively H0-bounded V or W, assume the graph estimate actually needed,
e.g. ||Vx||<=a||Ax||+b||x||, likewise W. Then
||VU2_delta||<=a||S||+b||U2_delta||, and the same conclusion follows.

3. ELECTRIC FIELD AND HALF-SPACE: INCLUDE THEM, THEN REPAIR THE NATIVE TRAP

The Maxwell electric field has |E|/|B|~omega/kappa. Its induced atomic
potential is order g^2 and therefore cannot be discarded on g^-2 times.
On the physical half-space F<=F_wall, however, all polynomial fields and
their Stark potentials are bounded. The whole-line negative F^4 instability
was an invalid extension through the source plane.

A cutoff from F8 to F16 was evaluated on the original complete rational
trial, including its finite u2, not just on the bare bound wavefunction.
At g=.001D its additional two-channel code error is about6.512e-6. A cutoff
from F4 to F8 gives a vacuous long-time bound; this failure is preserved.
The cutoff numbers do not transfer to the different full magnetic trial.

For a declared Rb87 M1 model, lambda8, hyperfine carrier6.834GHz and F_wall16,
a very loose all-37-electron nonrelativistic TRK bound puts the original
electric-potential norm-time allowance below6.2e-7. A measured scalar
polarizability gives a smaller estimate. No cancellation of compulsory
electric fields was assumed. A complete microscopic atomic-response and
noise certificate is a separate task.

Actual surface forces change the native potential even far from the wall.
With D/h=1kHz the native minimum is5.349micrometres from the F16 surface but
the g=.001 phase takes4186s. With D/h=100kHz those values become534.9nm and
41.86s. Setting the old dimensionless Delta_hf=100D using Rb would put the
minimum near20.46nm: the ideal Morse model cannot be casually reused there.

The next construction therefore uses an explicitly changed native operator:

 H_native/D=-(1/64)d_x^2+(1-F)^2
            -eta/max(x+ln16,1/2)^4,
 F=exp(-x), x>=-ln16, Dirichlet boundary.

The capped inner potential is a declared bounded continuation, not a claimed
short-distance Casimir--Polder law. Outside it the model uses a zero-
temperature ideal-conductor retarded CP potential. For eta=.019487..., the
actual continuum solutions and native eigenstates determine the matrix

 A_(n,r)=<E_n+Lambda,regular continuum |F^r|phi_n>.

Choose a real vector c in its nullspace; it cancels the three actual main
escape amplitudes. Ordinary one-channel energy regularity makes their simple
zeros normalizable divided sources. The continuum has not been discarded.

The original F,F2,F3,F4 choice FAILS as a robust correction basis
